findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the EC2 instance's user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 metadata service and Terraform state, risking credential theft and long-term compromise if leaked.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management interface of the instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.

The security group's egress rule allows all outbound traffic to any destination and protocol (0.0.0.0/0, all ports), which does not follow least privilege and could facilitate data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data stored on this disk is not encrypted at rest, violating data-at-rest protection requirements.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block / bucket policy restricting access, risking unauthorized access to network traffic metadata and unencrypted storage of sensitive log data.

The instance is deployed in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and attached to a security group permitting inbound SSH and HTTP from anywhere, directly exposing the compute instance to untrusted networks.
